As some of you already noticed, I have been on a little social media break lately. Don’t worry I am still here, it’s just that in the winter months it’s bit tougher to shoot floors. Light is bad, floors are dirty, wet and shiny. You also have to take good care of the precious shoes in these months. 
I am already thinking of doing another (maybe a last) floor series in another country. 
For the moment the Amalfi Coast with its unique handpainted ceramic tiles is high on my list. So if you have any recommendations for this area please send me a DM.
.

#marrakechfloors#parisianfloors#ihavethisthingwithfloors#fromwhereistand#selfeet#tiles#mosaic#pophamdesign#pattern#design#interiordesign#architecture#marrakech#louboutin#louboutinhomme

Making tiles with @pophamdesign
.
So here it finally is. My video showcasing the whole process of producing cement tiles:
- Mixing the colour pigments
- Preparing the cement mixture
- adding water to the colour pigment mixture
- cleaning the moulds and iron cast
- adding the layer of colour
- adding a mix of cement and ground marble as the back of the tile.
- leveling the back of the tile
- tiles get pressed under a hydraulic press
- carefully remove the tile from the iron cast
- finished tiles are cured in the “hammam” for 2.5 - 3 weeks; they gain strength by curing, which is the chemical reaction - between concrete and water.
.
Those 3 videos will give you an overview of the process and behind the scenes look of the atelier. (Don’t forget to swipe left to see all of them).
A big thank you to Caitlin & Samuel from @pophamdesign and all the people working there for making this amazing experience possible.
.
Music by @ashamaluevmusic & @djquads

- Marrakechfloors -

I didn’t just go for fun to Marrakech. I had an idea, something that I wanted to share with all of you. I always wanted to see how all these beautiful tiles that I photograph everywhere are made. So once we decided to go to Marrakech I reached out to Caitlin & Samuel from @pophamdesign, who are based in Marrakech and produce their beautiful tiles there. I asked them if they would be willing to show me around their atelier and explain me the process of making tiles. 
Not only did they give me full access to their atelier and spent the day with me showing me what it takes to produce tiles, they also had a little surprise for me. First I got to make a tile by myself and then they also invited me into their home in Marrakech. Let me tell you their home is a heaven for tileaddicts and an inspiration. 
Tomorrow i’ll show you some images in my stories of their beautiful home to give you some inspiration and an idea on how to use tiles in your home.
Then this weekend i’ll give you a full insight into the process of making tiles. I am really happy and thankful that I got this opportunity and I am more than excited to share it with you!
This image was taken in the showroom at their atelier.

We are back from a week roaming through Marrakech. For me it was a “back to the roots” experience, as Marrakech was the place that gave me the inspiration for the parisianfloors project. We start off at one of Marrakech’s most impressive hotels - La Mamounia. They not only have a beautiful garden but also some interesting traditional mosaic floors throughout the hotel. I am wearing some traditional “babouche” slippers that I found after some long strolls through the souk (local market).
I’ll post some more behind the scenes images from Marrakech in my Stories. So make sure toncheck them out!

node.text:
🇨🇺Cubanfloors🇨🇺
We have come to an end of the cuban floors series in collaboration with @gucci.
I hope all of you enjoyed this series as much as I did. I think it’s the best floor series I’ve shot so far.
I want give a big thank you to @gucci for supporting me on this and helping me realize a long term dream.
A even bigger thank you to all the lovely cubans that hosted us on our trip and that welcomed us in their homes and shared their experiences with us. Last but not least to my @lageorgienne ❤️
This is one of the floors that stood out most to me. During the whole trip we have encountered numerous floors with similar floral inspired designs or color palettes but this one was definitely different so was the location where we found this.
While strolling through the streets of Trinidad we stumbled upon a building with quite a big door and when we took a peek inside the room was filled with pregnant woman waiting for their appointment in their rocking chairs. We ended up at a maternity. I am not sure who was more surprised, us once we realized what we found or them once they saw what we were doing. It was definitely a funny sight and there was a lot of laughter when we explained that we take pictures of floors. 
If you haven’t seen the whole cuban floors series yet, go check my profile  and leave a comment on your favourite floors! 
Hope you enjoyed it!

#cubanfloors#gucci#gucciprincetown#trinidad#cuba#sponsored

My beautiful country. I still remember my grandmothers colonial house with these beautiful tiles and the high ceiling. They need me feel like if I was in a movie. Thank you for doing this beautiful series.

🇨🇺Cubanfloors🇨🇺
Here we go again with another beauty from Trinidad in collaboration with @gucci.
Trinidad is a real paradise for floors, but what makes it so special there is that they are pretty easy to spot. Most house in the historic center are 1 story homes with the living room being the room facing the street. So when you stroll through the cobble stone streets and you take a peek through the open windows, chances that you’ll see an incredible floor there are pretty high. On the plus side, the locals were super friendly and once we spotted a floor and asked if we could take a picture they were more than happy to let us in and show us around their home. They shared many stories with us and gave us a very personal insight into their live. A fact that made this trip very special for us.

#cubanfloors#gucci#gucciprincetown#cuba#trinidad#sponsored
Trinidad is amazing! Love seeing your photos.

The cuban floors series in collaboration with @gucci continues with another vibrant image of a floor from Trinidad!
We shot this one in a private cuban home. Trinidad has totally different vibe compared to Havana or Cienfuegos. It’s more calm and it feels a bit more like an ancient town that stopped at a moment in time. The historic old center is filled with colorful old houses and in the cobble stone streets you might not only encounter beautiful vintage cars but also many horse carriages. Still a reliable mode of transportation in the area. Check my Stories for impressions from Trinidad!

The day has come that I can finally present you my latest series in collaboration with @gucci. 
For 2 weeks @lageorgienne and I travelled through Cuba in search of the most beautiful old tile floors. We started in Havana, went over to Trinidad, passing by Santa Clara and then Cienfuegos circling back to Havana. In each city we were greeted by the most lovely and welcoming people, found incredible floors, ate our way through the local cuisine and had most most unforgettable experience in this extraordinary country. All of which we are gonna share with you over the next 2 weeks. Not only will I post 2 of my favorite floors every day!! but i will also share some exclusive behind the scenes images and videos of our journey! node.text:
Mont Saint-Michel

Found this floor on my recent trip to Normandy and Brittany. We went to see the Mont Saint-Michel and this floor was in one of the shops. I was a bit dissappointed by Mont Saint-Michel. It is beautiful to look at but inside there is not a lot to do except weird tourist shops and overprized restaurants. I wouldn't recommend doing s trip to just see the Mont Saint Michel but rather explore the beautiful countryside and areas around in Brittany and just make a quick stop to see Mont Saint-Michel.

I am happy to announce that for the 2nd anniversary of my project, I have a very 
special competition planned in collaboration with @etro. 
I want to challenge all of you during the next 7 days  to take a picture of the most beautiful floors in your city.
In the end I will pick 2 winners, who each will get a pair of choice from the current
Spring/Summer 2017 @etro shoe collection!! All you have to do to participate is:
- take a new picture with your feet and a floor
- upload it to your account
- add the following description and hashtag: “Happy 2 year anniversary @parisianfloors and I 
want to rock the new @etro shoes!
#EtroXparisianfloors”
- and tag @parisianfloors in the image

Reminder: 
Your account needs to be public to participate and you will need 
to follow all 4 steps mentioned above to successfully enter the competition.
The competition will end at midnight on Sunday the 28th of May 2017 (GMT+2)

@shernand24  You neeeeeed to follow this account!!!

🎊🎉 2 year anniversary 🎉🎊 Exactly 2 years ago I posted my first picture on this account. Now after 565 images later, I have probably shot over a few thousand floors in over 8 countries in Europe, met so many interesting people, discovered amazing hidden places and I don't even want to think about the hundreds (or maybe even more) kilometers I walked to take all this images. So today I am gonna post a little album with some memorable and special moments of my journey so far.
. ❤️A BIG THANK YOU to all of you for all the amazing support so far. You guys are the best!! ❤️
I wouldn't just celebrate this special day with a few images, but I also have an amazing competition lined up, which I will fully announce tomorrow!! So grab you shoes and get your cameras ready! 📷👞👠 Album captions:
1. Most liked picture

3. Filming with the german TV ZDF

node.text:
The last days I have encountered some really beautiful floors here in Valencia, but one definitely stood out. When @mireilalala told me that she had a beautiful floor in her apartment and that I could drop by to take a picture, I didn't really know what to expect. It is really rare now that I find a floor that makes me speechless after all I have seen so far but this one was special! .

As most of you might have already seen, I am currently in Valencia for a few days. The reason I am here is, that I got invited to the @cevisama (International trade fair for ceramics tiles, surface coatings and bathroom and kitchen facilities) in Valencia. I have a funny story for this floor. When I entered the shop and asked if I could take a picture of this floor, the owner asked me what I do with the picture. so i showed him my project. He was surprised and quickly grabbed a book in his shop,showed me some pages and asked me if it was me. I said yes. 2 weeks ago I spent a few days in Venice to work on a fun little project in collaboration with @pixartprinting . They invited me to come to Venice and explore the cities variety of marble and mosaic floors. During 3 days I walked a lot and by now I probably know all little streets of Venice.
